methods.name: QLoRA
methods.paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(target_modules='all-linear') on a model loaded with BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True) + prepare_model_for_kbit_training
methods.formula_latex: h=\mathrm{doubleDequant}\big(c_1^{\mathrm{FP32}},c_2^{\mathrm{FP8}},W_0^{\mathrm{NF4}}\big)\,x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx,\quad W_0^{\mathrm{NF4}}=q_{\mathrm{NF4}}(W_0)\ \text{frozen (blockwise, constants double-quantized)},\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained in BF16 (paged optimizer)}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: every linear layer of the transformer (attention and MLP); base weights stored as 4-bit NormalFloat
methods.structure: rank-r additive update BA on top of a frozen 4-bit NF4 (quantile-quantized, blockwise, double-quantized constants) base weight; storage dtype NF4, compute dtype BF16, so \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space while W_0 lives on a 16-level grid
methods.mergeable_reason: BA merges exactly only into a dequantized 16-bit copy of W_0; merging and re-quantizing to NF4 adds fresh rounding error, so exact inference at the original 4-bit cost is not preserved.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (LoRA default, A random), so the initial function is the quantized model \mathrm{dequant}(q_{NF4}(W_0)), not W_0: the quantization gap is left uncompensated at init (the gap LoftQ / LQ-LoRA / ApiQ close).
methods.key_idea: Backpropagate through a frozen 4-bit base model into LoRA adapters. Three memory tricks make this work: NF4 (a quantile data type that is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights), double quantization of the scale constants, and paged optimizers. Together they let a 65B model be fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU.
methods.results_note: Fine-tunes a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU while matching 16-bit fine-tuning; Guanaco-65B reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's score on the Vicuna benchmark after 24 hours on one GPU.

relations.note: LoRA adapters attached to a frozen NF4-quantized backbone
LoftQ with T=0 alternating steps (Q=q_N(W_0), BA=0) is exactly QLoRA's initialization
concurrent (May 2023) memory-efficient fine-tuning of quantized LLMs; PEQA tunes quantization scales instead of adding adapters
QA-LoRA removes QLoRA's need for a 16-bit merge / post-training re-quantization

methods.name: QA-LoRA
methods.paper_title: QA-LoRA: Quantization-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \tilde W_0=\alpha\odot(\hat W-z),\ \hat W\in\{0,\dots,2^b-1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{(GPTQ, one }(\alpha_{j,l},z_{j,l})\text{ per output }j\text{ and input group }l=1..L);\quad h=\tilde W_0x+s\,BA\,\mathrm{pool}_L(x),\ \ \mathrm{pool}_L(x)_l=\textstyle\sum_{i\in\mathcal G_l}x_i,\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times L},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r};\quad \text{merge: } z'_{j,l}=z_{j,l}-s\,(BA)_{j,l}/\alpha_{j,l}
methods.trainable_params: r\,(L+d_{out}),\quad L=d_{in}/g
methods.locus: all linear layers of the LLM (attention and MLP projections); base weights group-wise INT2/3/4 quantized with GPTQ
methods.structure: low-rank update constrained to be constant on each input quantization group: \Delta W=s\,BAP with P\in\{0,1\}^{L\times d_{in}} the group-summation operator, so rank\le r and \Delta W lies exactly in the span of per-group zero-point shifts
methods.mergeable_reason: Because \Delta W is constant across the g inputs of every quantization group, it is absorbed exactly into the per-group zero-points, giving a pure INT-b model at the original inference cost.
methods.identity_at_init: LoRA-style zero initialization of one factor (B = 0), so training starts from the GPTQ-quantized model rather than from W_0.
methods.key_idea: QA-LoRA rebalances the degrees of freedom of quantization and adaptation. Quantization parameters become finer (group-wise) and the LoRA input becomes coarser (group-pooled), so every learned update is exactly a shift of the quantizer's zero-points. The adapter therefore merges into an INT-b model without loss.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA/LLaMA2 (7B-65B), INT4 QA-LoRA matches mixed-precision QLoRA and beats QLoRA+GPTQ on MMLU and commonsense QA. The margin widens at low bit-widths, e.g. +15.0% average commonsense accuracy over post-quantized QLoRA at 2 bits on LLaMA-7B.

relations.note: same frozen-quantized-base + LoRA recipe, but quantization-aware so that the merged model stays integer
LoRA with the down-projection constrained to A' = AP (rows tied within input groups)
QA-LoRA effectively learns the quantizer's additive zero-points (through a low-rank factorization), PEQA learns its multiplicative scales
L4Q also yields a fully quantized merged model but without constraining the LoRA factors

methods.name: LoftQ
methods.paper_title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(init_lora_weights='loftq', loftq_config=LoftQConfig(loftq_bits=4, loftq_iter=1)); or replace_lora_weights_loftq(peft_model) on a bnb-4bit model
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\lVert W_0-Q-BA\rVert_F:\ \ Q_t=q_N(W_0-B_{t-1}A_{t-1}),\ \ B_tA_t=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q_t)\ (B_t=U_r\Sigma_r^{1/2},\ A_t=\Sigma_r^{1/2}V_r^{\top}),\ \ B_0A_0=0;\qquad h=(Q_T+BA)x,\ Q_T\ \text{frozen }N\text{-bit},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all targeted linear layers (best with target_modules='all-linear'); quantized backbone (NF4/NF2 or uniform)
methods.structure: W_0 \approx Q + BA: an N-bit matrix plus the rank-r truncated SVD of the quantization residual, found by alternating quantization and SVD; fine-tuning then trains the rank-r part
methods.mergeable_reason: As with QLoRA, BA can be merged exactly only into a high-precision copy of the weight; merging into the N-bit Q requires re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate rather than exact: Q_T+B_TA_T is the alternating best N-bit-plus-rank-r approximation of W_0, which strictly shrinks the quantization gap of QLoRA's Q+0; T=1 already helps and T=0 recovers QLoRA.
methods.key_idea: LoftQ makes quantization LoRA-aware. It picks the quantized backbone and the LoRA initialization jointly, so the adapter starts out cancelling the quantization error. This matters most at 2-3 bits, where zero-initialized QLoRA often fails to train.
methods.results_note: Never underperforms QLoRA across DeBERTaV3 (GLUE, SQuAD, ANLI), BART (XSum, CNN/DM) and LLaMA-2 (WikiText-2, GSM8K). At 2 bits it gains more than 8% on MNLI and more than 10% on SQuADv1.1.

relations.note: T=0 recovers QLoRA's zero-initialized adapters on q_N(W_0)
concurrent; same objective \min\lVert W_0-Q-BA\rVert, LQ-LoRA starts from Q^{(0)}=0 and adds ILP mixed precision and Fisher weighting
both use an SVD-based LoRA init; LoftQ uses the SVD of the quantization residual, PiSSA that of W_0 itself
ApiQ replaces LoftQ's weight-space objective by an activation-space objective

methods.name: LQ-LoRA
methods.paper_title: LQ-LoRA: Low-rank Plus Quantized Matrix Decomposition for Efficient Language Model Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q\in\mathbb{Q}_{c},\,B,A}\big\lVert\sqrt{F}\odot\big(W_0-(Q+BA)\big)\big\rVert_F\ \ (F\equiv\mathbf 1\ \text{or diagonal empirical Fisher}):\ \ B^{(t)}A^{(t)}=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q^{(t-1)}),\ \ Q^{(t)}=\mathrm{Quantize}_c(W_0-B^{(t)}A^{(t)}),\ Q^{(0)}=0;\ \ c=(\text{bits, block sizes})\ \text{per matrix from an ILP under a global bit budget};\quad h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all linear layers of the transformer, each with its own NF quantization configuration
methods.structure: robust-PCA-style low-rank-plus-quantized decomposition W_0 \approx Q + BA; Q uses a per-matrix mixed-precision configuration chosen by integer linear programming; data-aware variant uses a row/column-scaled (Fisher-weighted) SVD
methods.mergeable_reason: The low-rank component is high-precision and can be folded only into a dequantized copy of Q; folding into the quantized Q needs re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q+BA is the alternating approximation of W_0 (stopped when the error rises). Since Q^{(0)}=0, the first low-rank component is the top-r SVD of W_0 itself, so the adapter starts on W_0's principal subspace rather than at zero.
methods.key_idea: Split each pretrained matrix into a fixed, easily quantized part and a trainable high-variance low-rank part. Integer linear programming then allocates bits across matrices to meet any target memory budget.
methods.results_note: Beats QLoRA and GPTQ-LoRA at matched bit budgets on LLaMA-2 (C4, OpenAssistant) and RoBERTa-large (GLUE). For example, 3.5-bit Fisher LQ-LoRA roughly equals 4.127-bit NF4 QLoRA, and a 2.75-bit LLaMA-2-70B (27GB) stays competitive with 16-bit.

relations.note: same Q+BA objective; differs in starting point (Q^{(0)}=0 vs BA=0), ILP bit allocation and Fisher weighting
with the identity quantizer and one iteration, the decomposition is exactly PiSSA's principal-component adapter plus frozen residual
same frozen-quantized-base + LoRA fine-tuning stage

methods.name: IR-QLoRA
methods.paper_title: Accurate LoRA-Finetuning Quantization of LLMs via Information Retention
methods.formula_latex: \hat W_0=\mathrm{NF}k\!\Big(\tfrac{W_0-\tau^{*}}{\mathrm{absmax}(W_0-\tau^{*})}\Big)\,s+\tau^{*},\ \ \tau^{*}=\arg\max_{\tau}\ \mathcal H\big(\mathrm{NF}k((W_0-\tau)/s)\big)\ \text{(blockwise entropy search, double-quantized)};\quad h=\hat W_0x+\alpha\,U_2(U_1(x)),\ \ U_1(x)=Ax+\beta_1\,\mathrm{pool}_r(x),\ \ U_2(u)=Bu+\beta_2\,\mathrm{tile}_{d_{out}}(u)
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2
methods.locus: all linear layers of LLaMA/LLaMA2; NF2-NF4 or integer-quantized base
methods.structure: LoRA with parameter-free 'elastic' shortcuts: \Delta W=\alpha(B+\beta_2T)(A+\beta_1P), where P\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} averages contiguous input groups and T\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} tiles the r-vector; still rank \le r. Base is an entropy-calibrated NF-k quantizer with a per-block shift \tau
methods.mergeable_reason: The IEC shortcuts are linear and fold into the LoRA factors (and then into a 16-bit copy of the weight), but folding into the NF-k base requires re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA. The paper does not state how the learnable scalars \beta_1,\beta_2 are initialized (if \beta_2 \ne 0 the update is non-zero at step 0). The starting base is the ICQ-quantized model, not W_0.
methods.key_idea: View quantize-then-LoRA through information retention. Calibration Quantization (ICQ) maximizes the entropy of the quantized weights so they keep more information. The Elastic Connection (IEC) adds parameter-free pooling and tiling paths so LoRA can directly reuse the original features.
methods.results_note: Improves LLaMA/LLaMA2 at 2-4 bits over QLoRA and QA-LoRA, e.g. +1.4% MMLU for 4-bit LLaMA-7B over the prior state of the art, at only 0.31% extra training time.

relations.note: same NF-k + LoRA pipeline with a calibrated quantizer and augmented adapter
both route group-pooled inputs into the adapter; IR-QLoRA uses pooling as an extra shortcut, not as a constraint
both reduce the quantization gap at init, via entropy calibration rather than residual SVD

methods.name: L4Q
methods.full_name: Low-rank adaptive Learning quantization for LLMs
methods.paper_title: L4Q: Parameter Efficient Quantization-Aware Fine-Tuning on Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_{comb}=W_0+\alpha BA,\quad \tilde w=\mathrm{round}\Big(\mathrm{clamp}\big(\tfrac{W_{comb}-b}{s},Q_N,Q_P\big)\Big),\ \ W_q=\tilde w\,s+b,\quad h=W_qx;\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B,s,b)\ \text{trained with STE};\ \ \tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial B}=\alpha\big(\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial W_q}\odot\mathbb 1_{[Q_N,Q_P]}\big)A^{\top}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2\,d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \ \text{(LoRA factors + one scale and bias per quantization group of size } g)
methods.locus: all linear layers (LLaMA 7B-33B, OpenLLaMA-3B, Mistral-7B)
methods.structure: learned-step-size quantizer composed after a rank-r additive update: W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA); custom backward reuses \partial\mathcal L/\partial W_q so no weight-gradient buffer is stored
methods.mergeable_reason: The deployed model is exactly the fully quantized W_q=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA); no adapter or 16-bit branch remains at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0, so training starts from the 'L4Q init' symmetric quantization of W_0 (scale s=\max(|\min W/Q_N|,|\max W/Q_P|), chosen to avoid clipping outliers), not from W_0 itself.
methods.key_idea: Put the LoRA update inside the quantizer rather than beside it, and train LoRA jointly with the quantization scale and bias. The result is a fully quantized model without QA-LoRA's constraints on the factors, at roughly LoRA's training memory.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA and Mistral models with instruction data, 4-bit and 3-bit L4Q is more accurate than decoupled quantize-then-fine-tune schemes and QA-LoRA, at inference speed comparable to other fully quantized models.

relations.note: LoRA factors inside a quantization-aware training (LSQ-style) quantizer
both produce merged integer models; L4Q leaves A and B unconstrained by re-quantizing W_0+\alpha BA
both learn quantization scales; L4Q also learns a LoRA update inside the quantizer
both are memory-efficient quantization-aware training procedures for LLMs

methods.name: PEQA
methods.paper_title: Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Compressed Large Language Models via sub-4-bit Integer Quantization
methods.formula_latex: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s_0+\Delta s)\,\overline W_0,\quad \overline W_0=\mathrm{clamp}\big(\lfloor W_0/s_0\rceil+z_0,\,0,\,2^b-1\big)-z_0\ \ \text{(frozen integer codes)},\ \ s_0,z_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}};\ \ \text{only } s_0+\Delta s \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\ \text{(per-channel; } d_{out}\,d_{in}/g \text{ for group size } g)
methods.locus: every linear layer of a weight-only (3-4 bit) quantized LLM
methods.structure: diagonal rescaling of the output rows of a frozen integer matrix: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,\overline W_0 (group-wise: one scale per output row and input group); the integer codes never change
methods.mergeable_reason: The trained parameters are the quantization scales themselves, so the result is a standard quantized model with the same integer codes and kernels.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta s = 0: the model starts as the RTN/OPTQ-quantized model whose scales s_0 minimize \lVert W_0-\hat W_0\rVert_F, so the starting point is close to but not exactly W_0.
methods.key_idea: Treat the quantization step sizes as the PEFT parameters. Freeze the integer codes and fine-tune only per-channel scales, so each task adapter is a tiny scale vector and the deployed model stays quantized.
methods.results_note: Scales to LLaMA-65B. After instruction tuning, sub-4-bit PEQA models recover or exceed their full-precision language-modeling, few-shot in-context and comprehension performance.

relations.note: concurrent memory-efficient fine-tuning of quantized LLMs (scales vs adapters)
PEQA learns the quantizer's multiplicative scales, QA-LoRA its additive zero-points
algebraically the same diagonal output scaling as (IA)^3 (diag(s)\,W x), applied to every quantized linear layer and parameterized through the quantization scale
EfficientQAT's E2E-QP stage likewise trains only step sizes on frozen integer weights, after a block-wise reconstruction stage

methods.name: ApiQ
methods.paper_title: ApiQ: Finetuning of 2-Bit Quantized Large Language Model
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\ \big\lVert W_0X-(Q+BA)X^{q}\big\rVert_F\ \ \text{(layer-wise; block-wise: } \lVert\mathcal F(W_s,X)-\mathcal F(Q_s,A_s,B_s,X^{q})\rVert),\ \ Q=q_b(W_0;\gamma,\beta)\ \text{with learnable clipping }(\gamma,\beta)\ \text{via STE},\ X^{q}=\text{inputs from the already-quantized preceding layers};\ \text{then fine-tune } h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{during fine-tuning}
methods.locus: all linear layers (or whole transformer blocks for ApiQ-bw); DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa, Llama-2, Mistral
methods.structure: the same Q+BA shape as LoftQ, but fitted in activation space with calibration data, sequentially layer-by-layer or block-by-block so that quantization error does not accumulate with depth
methods.mergeable_reason: BA can be merged only into a high-precision copy; merging into the b-bit Q requires re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q, A, B are calibrated so that the quantized layer or block reproduces the full-precision activations given the already-quantized inputs X^{q}; the model function is close to, not equal to, the original.
methods.key_idea: Initialize LoRA and quantize jointly by matching activations, not weights. Each quantized layer is fitted given its quantized inputs, so the adapter stops error propagation from shallow to deep layers, which is crucial at 2 bits.
methods.results_note: Attains the lowest activation error and the best fine-tuning results against QLoRA, LoftQ and LQ-LoRA across 2-4 bits on GLUE (DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa) and on Llama-2/Mistral language modeling, arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, with the largest gains at 2 bits.

relations.note: same joint (Q,A,B) initialization, objective moved from weight error \lVert W_0-Q-BA\rVert to activation error
alternative quantization-aware LoRA initialization
replaces QLoRA's zero-init adapters on a naively quantized base

methods.name: EfficientQAT
methods.paper_title: EfficientQAT: Efficient Quantization-Aware Training for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \text{Block-AP: }\min_{W,s,z}\lVert\mathcal F_{blk}(W_0,X)-\mathcal F_{blk}(Q_{s,z}(W),X)\rVert\ \text{block by block};\quad \text{E2E-QP: } \hat W=s\odot(\overline W-z),\ \overline W\ \text{frozen integers},\ \text{only step sizes } s \text{ trained end-to-end on the task loss}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \text{step sizes in E2E-QP (group size } g)
methods.locus: all linear layers of the LLM; 2-4 bit group-wise uniform quantization
methods.structure: two stages: block-wise reconstruction training of all weights plus quantization parameters, then end-to-end training of group-wise multiplicative step sizes only (diagonal-per-group scaling of a frozen integer matrix)
methods.mergeable_reason: Training only changes integer codes (Block-AP) and step sizes (E2E-QP), so the output is a standard group-wise quantized model.
methods.identity_at_init: E2E-QP starts from the Block-AP-calibrated quantized model (step sizes from Block-AP); there is no exact identity with W_0, by design of quantization.
methods.key_idea: Make quantization-aware training feasible for 70B models in two stages. First, train all parameters block by block against a reconstruction loss. Then, end to end, train only the quantization step sizes, which is a PEQA-style parameter-efficient stage on a frozen integer model.
methods.results_note: Produces a 2-bit Llama-2-70B on a single A100-80GB in 41 hours with less than 3 points of accuracy loss (69.48 vs 72.41), and outperforms prior quantization methods from 7B to 70B, including instruction-tuned and multimodal LLMs.

relations.note: the E2E-QP stage trains only quantization scales on frozen integer weights, like PEQA
both are memory-efficient QAT for LLMs
alternative route to accurate low-bit fine-tuned models without a 16-bit branch

methods.name: LoQT
methods.paper_title: LoQT: Low-Rank Adapters for Quantized Pretraining
methods.formula_latex: h=\big(W_Q+s\,P_QB\big)x,\ \ W_Q=q_{NF4}(W),\ \ P=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{from}\ \mathrm{SVD}(\nabla_W\mathcal L)\ \text{(frozen, } P_Q=q_{NF4}(P)),\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained},\ B_{init}\approx P^{+}(W-q_{NF4}(W));\quad \text{at } t\in\{T_i\}:\ W\leftarrow W_Q+sP_QB,\ \text{recompute }P,\ \text{re-quantize, re-init }B;\ \ T_{i}=\tau+\psi^{i}
methods.trainable_params: r\,d_{in}\ \text{(only } B\text{; } W \text{ and } P \text{ frozen and quantized; projector shown on the output side, } r\,d_{out} \text{ if placed on the input side)}
methods.locus: all attention and MLP linear layers; used for both pre-training and fine-tuning
methods.structure: one-sided low-rank adapter with a frozen gradient-derived projector, W=W_Q+sPB with P the top-r left singular vectors of \nabla_W\mathcal L; periodically merged into the NF4 weight and re-quantized at exponentially growing intervals
methods.mergeable_reason: PB is periodically merged into the (quantized) full-rank weight, with a final merge at the end, so inference uses a plain dense or quantized matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: B is initialized to compensate the quantization error (B \approx P^{+}(W-q_{NF4}(W))) instead of 0; without quantization (LoQT-nq), B=0 gives exact identity.
methods.key_idea: Realize GaLore's projected step as a trainable adapter. Freeze a gradient-SVD projector P and train only B in W+PB; since \partial\mathcal L/\partial B=P^{\top}\nabla_W\mathcal L, Adam on B equals GaLore within a window. Periodically fold PB into an NF4 weight, so neither W nor P ever needs 16-bit storage or gradients.
methods.results_note: Trains models up to 7B on a single 24GB GPU (13B with per-layer gradient updates). Perplexity is close to unquantized low-rank baselines in LLaMA pre-training on C4, with competitive DeBERTaV3 GLUE and GSM8K fine-tuning.

relations.note: without quantization and within one interval, Adam on B in W+PB applies P\,\rho(P^{\top}G), exactly GaLore's one-sided projected update with the same P
periodic merging of low-rank factors into the base weight to accumulate a high-rank update
NF4 quantization of the frozen weight (and here also of the projector)
both train only one factor of a low-rank product with the other frozen (random A in LoRA-FA, gradient-SVD P in LoQT)

methods.name: GaLore
methods.paper_title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
methods.formula_latex: G_t=\nabla_W\mathcal L(W_t)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}},\ \ P_t=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{of}\ \mathrm{SVD}(G_{t_0})\ \text{(refreshed every }T\text{ steps)};\ \ R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ (M_t,V_t)=\mathrm{Adam}(R_t),\ N_t=M_t/(\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon);\quad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_tN_t\ \ \text{(all of }W\text{ trained; no adapter; shown for } d_{out}\le d_{in}\text{, else project on the right)}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state } 2r\,d_{in}+r\,d_{out}\ \text{vs. } 2d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{for Adam (for } d_{out}\le d_{in})
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices of attention and MLP blocks (embeddings / LM head usually kept on standard Adam)
methods.structure: each step's update lies in an r-dimensional left subspace: \Delta W_t=-\eta\alpha P_tN_t with P_t\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r) the gradient's top singular vectors; the subspace switches every T steps, so the accumulated \sum_t\Delta W_t is high-rank
methods.mergeable_reason: There is no auxiliary module: updates are written straight into W, so the result is an ordinary dense checkpoint with the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: training starts at W_0 with no reparameterization; the projector is initialized from the SVD of the first gradient.
methods.key_idea: Put the low-rank structure on the gradient rather than the weights. Project each gradient onto a periodically refreshed top-r singular subspace, run Adam there, and project back. This gives full-parameter learning with LoRA-like optimizer memory.
methods.results_note: Cuts optimizer-state memory by up to 65.5% (82.5% with 8-bit GaLore) while matching full-rank LLaMA 1B/7B pre-training on C4 (up to 19.7B tokens) and RoBERTa GLUE fine-tuning. It was the first to pre-train a 7B model on a single 24GB RTX 4090 without model parallelism, checkpointing or offloading.

relations.note: LoRA confines the weight update to a fixed r-dimensional subspace (parameter side); GaLore confines each gradient step to a periodically re-chosen r-dimensional subspace (optimizer side)
both aim at high-rank updates with low-rank memory, by periodic merging (ReLoRA) vs periodic subspace switching (GaLore)
SVD-chosen vs resampled random projections of the gradient
a frozen-P adapter W+PB trained with Adam reproduces GaLore's update inside one subspace window

methods.name: GaLore 2
methods.paper_title: GaLore 2: Large-Scale LLM Pre-Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
methods.formula_latex: W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_t\,\rho_t\big(P_t^{\top}G_t\big),\ \ P_t=\mathrm{rSVD}_r(G_{t_0})\ \text{(fast randomized SVD, refreshed every }T\text{ steps)};\ \rho_t=\text{(8-bit) Adam on the }r\times d_{in}\text{ state};\ \text{per-layer fused update after FSDP reduce-scatter; optional low-bit projectors (Q-GaLore) and tensor projections (Tensor-GaLore)}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state } \approx 2r\,d_{in}+r\,d_{out}
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices; designed for large-scale pre-training under FSDP
methods.structure: same projected-gradient structure as GaLore (\Delta W_t\in\mathrm{span}(P_t)\otimes\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}), with randomized-SVD projectors and sharded per-layer updates
methods.mergeable_reason: Updates go directly into W; the output is a standard dense checkpoint.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: starts at the initial (or pretrained) W with no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: An engineering consolidation of GaLore. Randomized SVD removes the SVD bottleneck (up to 20 minutes per subspace update on Llama 7B), FSDP integration fuses per-layer projected updates, and Q-GaLore and Tensor-GaLore extensions are folded in. The paper then tests GaLore at real pre-training scale.
methods.results_note: Pre-trains Llama 7B from scratch on 500B tokens with final validation loss, perplexity and downstream scores comparable to an 8-bit Adam baseline.

relations.note: same projected-gradient optimizer, made scalable (randomized SVD, FSDP)

methods.name: Q-GaLore
methods.paper_title: Q-GaLore: Quantized GaLore with INT4 Projection and Layer-Adaptive Low-Rank Gradients
methods.formula_latex: W^{\mathrm{INT8}}_{t+1}=\mathrm{SR}_{8}\Big(W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_t^{\mathrm{INT4}}\,\rho_t\big(P_t^{\mathrm{INT4}\top}G_t\big)\Big),\ \ \mathrm{SR}=\text{stochastic rounding (unbiased)};\ \ P_t^{\mathrm{INT4}}\ \text{block-wise INT4};\ \text{SVD interval of layer } l \text{ doubled when } \cos(P^{(l)}_{k\text{ intervals}})\ge\text{threshold (lazy layer-adaptive refresh)};\ \text{fused per-layer backward update}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight, stored INT8); optimizer state } \approx 2r\,d_{in}\ \text{(+ INT4 projector } r\,d_{out})
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices; pre-training and fine-tuning
methods.structure: GaLore projected update with quantized operands: INT8 weights updated through stochastic rounding, INT4 projector, per-layer adaptive subspace-refresh schedule
methods.mergeable_reason: Training directly updates the (INT8) weights; no adapter remains.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: starts from the (INT8-quantized) initial weights with no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Gradient subspaces settle early in many layers and projectors tolerate 4-bit quantization. Q-GaLore therefore refreshes subspaces lazily per layer, stores projectors in INT4 and weights in INT8, and uses stochastic rounding so small updates are not lost.
methods.results_note: Pre-trains LLaMA-7B from scratch on a single 16GB RTX 4060 Ti. In fine-tuning it uses up to 50% less memory than LoRA and GaLore and beats QLoRA by up to 5.19 MMLU points at the same memory cost.

relations.note: quantized, lazily refreshed GaLore
memory-matched fine-tuning comparison on MMLU

methods.name: Flora
methods.paper_title: Flora: Low-Rank Adapters Are Secretly Gradient Compressors
methods.formula_latex: \text{LoRA dynamics} \approx W_0-\eta\textstyle\sum_t G_tA_0^{\top}A_0\ \ (\text{random } A_0);\ \ \text{Flora: } C_t=G_tA_t^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\tfrac1r)^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{resampled per cycle};\ \ M_t=\beta M_{t-1}A_{t-1}A_t^{\top}+(1-\beta)C_t\ \text{(momentum transfer)};\ \ W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\mathcal U(M_tA_t)\ \ (\mathcal U=\text{base optimizer, Adafactor in the paper})
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); compressed state } r\,d_{out}\ \text{per EMA / accumulator (+ a random seed for } A_t)
methods.locus: attention and feed-forward weight matrices (embeddings and vector parameters handled uncompressed); T5, GPT-2 (ViT in the appendix)
methods.structure: random-projection (Johnson-Lindenstrauss) compression of the gradient along its input dimension, C=GA^{\top}, decompressed by CA; resampling A_t makes the accumulated update high-rank; sublinear O(r\,d_{out}) state
methods.mergeable_reason: Flora is an optimizer that writes directly into W; no adapter is created.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: W starts at W_0; only optimizer states are compressed.
methods.key_idea: Under SGD with a small learning rate, LoRA's update is dominated by B moving under a nearly fixed random A_0, i.e. -\eta GA_0^{\top}A_0, which is random-projection compression of the gradient. Resampling the projection breaks LoRA's low-rank ceiling while keeping its sublinear memory for momentum and gradient accumulation.
methods.results_note: With Adafactor as base optimizer, Flora-compressed gradient accumulation matches full-matrix accumulation on T5 (XSum) and GPT-2 (IWSLT17 De-En) at reasonably large r, using only about 30% of its memory overhead for T5-3B / GPT-2-XL at r=256. Compressed momentum recovers or surpasses naive momentum when training from scratch, where LoRA lags badly.

relations.note: shows LoRA updates are approximately random-projection gradient compressors (parameter-side LoRA = optimizer-side compression)
LoRA-FA (frozen random A, trained B) is Flora with a fixed, never-resampled projection under SGD
random (Flora) vs SVD-based (GaLore) gradient projections

methods.name: Fira
methods.full_name: Fira (full-rank training under a low-rank constraint)
methods.paper_title: Fira: Can We Achieve Full-rank Training of LLMs Under Low-rank Constraint?
methods.formula_latex: R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t,\ \ W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,P_t\psi_t(R_t)-\eta\,\big(G_t-P_tR_t\big)\,\mathrm{diag}\big(\phi_t(R_t)\big),\ \ \phi_t(R_t)_i=\frac{\lVert\psi_t(R_{t,:,i})\rVert}{\lVert R_{t,:,i}\rVert}\ \text{(column-wise)};\ \ \text{limiter: if } \lVert S_t\rVert/\lVert S_{t-1}\rVert>\gamma,\ S_t\leftarrow\gamma\lVert S_{t-1}\rVert\,S_t/\lVert S_t\rVert,\ \ S_t=(G_t-P_tR_t)\,\mathrm{diag}(\phi_t(R_t))
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight, full-rank gradient); optimizer state } \approx 2r\,d_{in}+r\,d_{out}\ \text{(as GaLore)}
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices; pre-training and fine-tuning
methods.structure: GaLore's Adam-in-subspace term plus the out-of-subspace gradient residual (I-P_tP_t^{\top})G_t rescaled column-wise by the low-rank Adam norm ratio, with a relative norm-growth limiter
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; updates go directly into W.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Adam's effect on gradient norms (the norm ratio before and after correction) is nearly the same in a low-rank subspace and in full rank. Fira reuses the cheap low-rank ratio to scale the discarded residual gradient, giving full-rank updates at low-rank memory, and adds a norm-growth limiter against loss spikes.
methods.results_note: Beats LoRA and GaLore in LLaMA pre-training and fine-tuning, matching or exceeding full-rank training. In LLaMA-7B pre-training it uses 8x less optimizer-state memory than GaLore and outperforms it by a large margin.

relations.note: setting the residual scale \phi_t\equiv0 recovers GaLore
concurrent use of channel-wise l2-norm-ratio scaling; APOLLO derives it from structured learning rates with random projections

methods.name: APOLLO
methods.full_name: Approximated Gradient Scaling for Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization
methods.paper_title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
methods.formula_latex: R_t=P_tG_t,\ P_t\sim\mathcal N_{seed}(0,\tfrac1r)^{r\times d_{out}}\ \text{(resampled every }T);\ \ (M^R_t,V^R_t)=\mathrm{AdamW}(R_t),\ \tilde R_t=M^R_t/(\sqrt{V^R_t}+\epsilon);\ \ s_j=\frac{\lVert\tilde R_t[:,j]\rVert_2}{\lVert R_t[:,j]\rVert_2}\ \text{(APOLLO; APOLLO-Mini: one tensor-wise } s=\lVert\tilde R_t\rVert/\lVert R_t\rVert,\ r=1);\quad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,G_t\,\mathrm{diag}(s)-\eta\lambda W_t
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state } 2r\,d_{in}\ \text{(}r=1\text{ for APOLLO-Mini, i.e. } 2d_{in}\text{: SGD-like)}
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices of attention and MLP (optim_target_modules)
methods.structure: structured (channel-wise or tensor-wise) learning-rate scaling: the raw full-rank gradient is right-multiplied by a diagonal matrix diag(s) whose entries are estimated from Adam states kept in a random r-dimensional sketch
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; produces an ordinary dense checkpoint.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: AdamW's element-wise adaptive learning rate is redundant and can be coarsened to one rate per channel or per tensor. Those few scaling factors can be estimated from Adam run inside a cheap random projection without SVD, even of rank 1.
methods.results_note: Matches or beats AdamW in LLaMA 60M-7B pre-training (up to 2.8 lower validation perplexity) at near-SGD memory, with about 3x throughput on 8xA100 from larger batches. APOLLO-Mini plus weight quantization pre-trains LLaMA-7B in 12GB.

methods.name: Online Subspace Descent
methods.paper_title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Online Subspace Descent
methods.formula_latex: W_{t+1}=W_t+P_t\,\phi_t(\hat S_t),\ \ \hat S_t=\psi_t\big(\hat S_{t-1},P_t^{\top}\nabla\mathcal L(W_t)\big);\ \ P_{t+1}=\mathrm{OptimizerP.step}\big(P_t,\nabla_P\mathcal L_{G_t}(P_t)\big),\ \ \mathcal L_{G}(P)=\lVert PP^{\top}\tilde G-\tilde G\rVert^2+\lambda\lVert P^{\top}P-I_r\rVert^2,\ \tilde G=G/\lVert G\rVert

methods.structure: projected optimizer whose projector P_t evolves continuously by one online-PCA gradient step per iteration (no SVD); any Hamiltonian-descent optimizer (SGD, momentum, Lion, Adam) can run inside the subspace
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; updates go directly into W.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Replace GaLore's periodic SVD with streaming online PCA on the projector. A Hamiltonian-descent (Lyapunov) analysis then gives the first convergence guarantee for arbitrary projector update rules.
methods.results_note: In LLaMA 60M-7B pre-training on C4 it reaches lower perplexity and better downstream scores than other low-rank training methods, narrowing the gap to full-rank baselines.

methods.name: Adam-mini
methods.paper_title: Adam-mini: Use Fewer Learning Rates To Gain More
methods.formula_latex: \theta=(\theta_{b})_{b\in\mathcal B}\ \text{(blocks = smallest dense Hessian sub-blocks: q,k by head; v, attn.proj, MLP by output neuron; embed/output by token)};\ \ m_b\leftarrow\beta_1m_b+(1-\beta_1)g_b,\ \ v_b\leftarrow\beta_2v_b+(1-\beta_2)\,\mathrm{mean}(g_b\odot g_b)\in\mathbb{R},\ \ \theta_b\leftarrow\theta_b-\eta\,m_b/(\sqrt{v_b}+\epsilon)
methods.trainable_params: \text{all parameters; second-moment state reduced from } d_{out}d_{in} \text{ to at most } d_{out}\ \text{scalars per matrix (one per block: per head for } W_q,W_k\text{, per output neuron otherwise)}
methods.locus: all parameters; Hessian-structure-aware partition of Transformer weights
methods.structure: block-wise shared adaptive learning rate: Adam's per-coordinate v is replaced by one scalar per Hessian block (more than 99.9% of v removed)
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; trains the original parameters directly.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Transformer Hessians are near block-diagonal, and one good learning rate per dense block is enough. Adam-mini keeps momentum but stores one second-moment scalar per block, halving Adam's optimizer memory.
methods.results_note: On par with or better than AdamW for 39M-13B models in pre-training, SFT and RLHF, with 50% less optimizer memory and 49.6% higher throughput for Llama 2-7B pre-training on 2xA800.

relations.note: both coarsen Adam's element-wise learning rates into structured ones

methods.name: MeZO
methods.paper_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
methods.trainable_params: \text{all } d \text{ parameters (or a PEFT subset such as LoRA / prefix); optimizer memory } O(1)\text{: one scalar and one seed}
methods.locus: all parameters (full-parameter) or the parameters of a PEFT module
methods.structure: SPSA zeroth-order estimate: a rank-one random projection zz^{\top}\nabla\mathcal L of the gradient, obtained from a finite difference of two forward passes; perturbations regenerated from a random seed so no extra memory is stored
methods.mergeable_reason: MeZO only changes how updates are computed; the trained parameters are the model's own (or a standard PEFT module).
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Classical ZO-SGD can run in place by regenerating Gaussian perturbations from a seed, so fine-tuning costs only inference memory. Good pre-training gives a low effective Hessian rank, so convergence does not degrade with parameter count.
methods.results_note: With one A100-80GB it fine-tunes a 30B model where backprop fits only 2.7B. It is comparable to backprop fine-tuning on many tasks (OPT up to 66B) with up to 12x memory reduction, works with LoRA and prefix-tuning, and can optimize non-differentiable objectives.

relations.note: MeZO can optimize LoRA parameters (MeZO-LoRA)
MeZO can optimize prefix parameters (MeZO-prefix)

methods.name: LOMO
methods.paper_title: Full Parameter Fine-tuning for Large Language Models with Limited Resources
methods.formula_latex: \text{during backprop, as soon as } g_i=\nabla_{\theta_i}\mathcal L \text{ is computed: } \theta_i\leftarrow\theta_i-\eta\,g_i,\ \text{then free } g_i\ \ \text{(fused gradient computation + SGD update; no optimizer state; gradient memory } O(\max_i|\theta_i|))

methods.locus: all parameters (full-parameter fine-tuning)
methods.structure: plain SGD whose per-tensor update is fused into the backward pass (layer-wise gradient release), plus gradient normalization and dynamic loss scaling for mixed precision
methods.mergeable_reason: Trains the original parameters directly; no extra modules.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: For fine-tuning, SGD works well enough to drop Adam's states entirely. Fusing each tensor's update into backpropagation also removes the full gradient buffer, leaving parameters and activations as the only memory.
methods.results_note: Combined with other memory-saving techniques it cuts memory to 10.8% of the DeepSpeed baseline, enabling full-parameter fine-tuning of a 65B model on one machine with 8x RTX 3090 (24GB).

relations.note: AdaLomo adds Adafactor-style factored second moments and grouped update normalization to LOMO's fused update

alternative memory-efficient full-parameter fine-tuning

methods.name: AdaLomo
methods.full_name: Low-memory Optimization with Adaptive Learning Rate
methods.paper_title: AdaLomo: Low-memory Optimization with Adaptive Learning Rate
methods.formula_latex: \text{fused in backprop, per matrix } \theta_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\ r_{t}=\beta r_{t-1}+(1-\beta)(g_t^{2})\mathbf 1_n,\ \ c_t=\beta c_{t-1}+(1-\beta)\mathbf 1_m^{\top}(g_t^{2}),\ \ v_t=r_tc_t/(\mathbf 1_m^{\top}r_t);\ \ u_t=g_t/\sqrt{v_t},\ \ \hat u_t=\frac{u_t}{\max(1,\mathrm{RMS}(u_t))}\max(\epsilon,\mathrm{RMS}(\theta_{t-1})),\ \ \theta_t=\theta_{t-1}-\alpha_t\hat u_t
methods.trainable_params: \text{all parameters; optimizer state } d_{out}+d_{in}\ \text{per matrix (factored second moment), no momentum}
methods.locus: all parameters (full-parameter instruction tuning and (further) pre-training)
methods.structure: rank-one non-negative factorization of the second-moment matrix (Adafactor-style row/column statistics) with grouped RMS update normalization, fused into the backward pass
methods.mergeable_reason: Trains the original parameters directly.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Of Adam's two ingredients, the adaptive learning rate matters more than momentum for closing LOMO's gap to AdamW. AdaLomo adds a factored, sublinear-memory second moment and a grouped normalization compatible with fused, single-pass backward updates. (The paper's Algorithm 1 writes u=g/v; the derivation in its Sec. 3 uses g/\sqrt{\hat v}.)
methods.results_note: Matches AdamW in instruction tuning, further pre-training and from-scratch pre-training of LLaMA models with LOMO-level memory.

methods.name: BAdam
methods.paper_title: BAdam: A Memory Efficient Full Parameter Optimization Method for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \theta=(\theta_{\pi_1},\dots,\theta_{\pi_D})\ \text{(e.g. one block per transformer layer; ascending / descending / random order)};\ \ \theta_{\pi_i}^{t+1}\approx\arg\min_{\theta_{\pi_i}}\mathcal L\big(\theta_{\pi_{<i}}^{t+1},\theta_{\pi_i},\theta_{\pi_{>i}}^{t}\big)\ \text{via } K \text{ Adam steps; other blocks frozen; Adam state of } \theta_{\pi_i} \text{ discarded when switching}

methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.

methods.name: LISA
methods.paper_title: LISA: Layerwise Importance Sampling for Memory-Efficient Large Language Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{every } K \text{ steps sample active layers with } p=\{1,\tfrac{\gamma}{N_L},\dots,\tfrac{\gamma}{N_L},1\}\ \text{(embedding and LM head always on, } \gamma \text{ of } N_L \text{ middle layers)};\ \ \theta_{\ell}\leftarrow\mathrm{AdamW}(\theta_\ell)\ \text{for active } \ell,\ \text{all other layers frozen}

methods.name: LoRA-FA
methods.paper_title: LoRA-FA: Memory-efficient Low-rank Adaptation for Large Language Models Fine-tuning
methods.hf_peft_config: peft.optimizers.create_lorafa_optimizer(model, r, lora_alpha, lr) on a LoraConfig model
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+s\,BA_0,\ \ s=\tfrac{\alpha}{r},\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random and frozen},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained with}\ \ \tilde g_B=\tfrac{1}{s^{2}}\,\nabla_B\mathcal L\,(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}\ \Rightarrow\ s\,\tilde g_BA_0=G\,A_0^{\top}(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}A_0=\arg\min_{\hat g\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}A_0}\lVert\hat g-G\rVert_F,\ \ G=\nabla_W\mathcal L

papers.title: Gradient Descent Happens in a Tiny Subspace
papers.claim: After a short period of training, the gradient converges to a very small subspace spanned by the top few Hessian eigenvectors (about as many as there are classes) and stays there.
papers.relevance: Empirical basis for the 'dual' (gradient-side) PEFT view: if the gradient flow is effectively low-dimensional, projecting gradients (GaLore, Flora, APOLLO) or confining updates to low-rank parameter subspaces (LoRA) loses little. It also explains why projector refresh schedules matter.

papers.title: Adafactor: Adaptive Learning Rates with Sublinear Memory Cost
papers.claim: Adam's per-parameter second moment for a weight matrix can be replaced by its row and column sums (a rank-one factorization), cutting optimizer memory from O(nm) to O(n+m) with similar results. Update clipping and an increasing decay rate fix the resulting instability.
papers.relevance: The prototype of optimizer-state compression: factoring the second moment is the optimizer-side counterpart of factoring the weight update. It is reused directly by Flora and AdaLomo and shares a lineage with Adam-mini, APOLLO and GaLore-Adafactor.

papers.title: 8-bit Optimizers via Block-wise Quantization
papers.claim: Block-wise dynamic quantization, combined with a stable embedding layer, lets Adam and momentum states be stored in 8 bits with no loss in performance, removing about 75% of optimizer-state memory.
papers.relevance: Shows that optimizer states, not just weights, can be quantized. Its block-wise quantization and paging infrastructure (bitsandbytes) underlies QLoRA's paged optimizers, 8-bit GaLore, and the 8-bit Adam baseline of GaLore 2.

papers.title: Subspace Optimization for Large Language Models with Convergence Guarantees
papers.claim: GaLore does not always converge to a stationary point in the stochastic setting: SVD projectors become noise-dominated when the true gradient is small, as an explicit counterexample shows. It does converge with large batches or isotropic noise. GoLore, which samples random projections uniformly from the Stiefel manifold, provably converges at standard batch sizes.
papers.relevance: Gives the projector-selection morphism of gradient-side PEFT a precise convergence semantics. Data-dependent (SVD) projectors and data-independent (random) projectors behave differently, which explains the shift toward random or online projectors (Flora, APOLLO, Online Subspace Descent).

papers.title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning: A Benchmark
papers.claim: A benchmark of BP-free zeroth-order fine-tuning across five LLM families, three task difficulties and five fine-tuning schemes. It finds that task alignment and the forward-gradient method matter, and proposes block-wise descent, hybrid ZO/FO training and gradient sparsity to improve ZO fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Maps the design space around MeZO and shows that ZO estimators combine naturally with parameter-side PEFT (LoRA, prefix). That makes the zeroth-order axis composable with the parametrization axis in a unified theory.

notes: Scope: quantization-aware PEFT (QLoRA, QA-LoRA, LoftQ, LQ-LoRA, IR-QLoRA, L4Q, PEQA, ApiQ, EfficientQAT, LoQT) and gradient-side memory-efficient training (GaLore, GaLore 2, Q-GaLore, Flora, Fira, APOLLO, Online Subspace Descent, Adam-mini, MeZO, LOMO, AdaLomo, BAdam, LISA, LoRA-FA). Key structural observations for the category-theoretic site: (1) Duality theorem (exact). For a one-sided-frozen adapter W=W_0+PB with P frozen, dL/dB = P^T dL/dW, so any optimizer on B applies P*rho(P^T G) to W. LoRA-FA is therefore projected gradient descent with a fixed random right-projector, LoQT within one interval is exactly GaLore, and Flora is the resampled version. This is a clean natural correspondence between the parameter side (adapters) and the optimizer side (gradient projections). (2) The quantizer has two kinds of parameters, which give two dual PEFT families. Additive zero-points: QA-LoRA's group-pooled LoRA lands exactly in the zero-point space. Multiplicative scales: PEQA and EfficientQAT's E2E-QP, algebraically (IA)^3-type diagonal scaling. L4Q composes the quantizer after the LoRA update, W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+BA). (3) Quantization-aware initializations solve variants of min ||W_0 - Q - BA||: weight space for LoftQ and LQ-LoRA, with Fisher weighting in LQ-LoRA; activation space for ApiQ; entropy-maximizing quantizer for IR-QLoRA. QLoRA is the T=0 point, and with an identity quantizer LQ-LoRA reduces to PiSSA. (4) Mergeability: methods whose update lives in the quantizer's parameter space (QA-LoRA, PEQA, L4Q, EfficientQAT) merge into an integer model exactly. QLoRA, LoftQ, LQ-LoRA, IR-QLoRA and ApiQ merge exactly only into a 16-bit copy ('conditional'). Optimizer-side methods are trivially 'mergeable' because they write into W. Integration facts (not HF PEFT): GaLore (optim='galore_adamw'/'galore_adamw_8bit'/'galore_adafactor', '_layerwise'), APOLLO (optim='apollo_adamw', APOLLO-Mini via optim_args rank=1, scale_type=tensor), and LOMO/AdaLomo (optim='lomo'/'adalomo') are Hugging Face transformers Trainer optimizers. In HF PEFT: QLoRA via bitsandbytes + prepare_model_for_kbit_training; LoftQ via init_lora_weights='loftq' or replace_lora_weights_loftq; QA-LoRA via LoraConfig(use_qalora=True) (GPTQ only); LoRA-FA via peft.optimizers.create_lorafa_optimizer. PEFT also supports quantized bases via GPTQ, AQLM, EETQ, HQQ, torchao, INC (FP8) and Transformer Engine, and VeRA, AdaLoRA and (IA)^3 with bnb. Uncertainties: IR-QLoRA's initialization of the learnable IEC scalars beta_1, beta_2 is not stated in the paper. AdaLomo's Algorithm 1 prints u=g/v while its derivation uses g/sqrt(v); I wrote sqrt. LoRA-FA arXiv v3 (May 2026) adds the closed-form gradient correction (r/alpha)^2 (A A^T)^{-1}, which v1 (2023) lacked, and has no formal venue. GaLore 2 is a tech report with no confirmed code release (the GaLore repo only announces it). Fira's NeurIPS 2025 venue is confirmed by its NeurIPS 2025 poster page. Overlaps with other families (same ids used for merging): qlora, qa-lora, loftq, lora-fa (hf-peft / lora-core / init-rank), and badam, lisa (selective). The id 'flora-opt' deliberately differs from 'flora-batched' and 'flora-tucker' in other families. Relations reference ids from other families: lora, pissa, relora, ia3, prefix-tuning, lora-pro, riemannian-preconditioned-lora. Notable members omitted for low uptake or redundancy: Tensor-GaLore, GaLore-mini, LDAdam, SubTrack++, GoLore (treated as a theory paper), MeZO variants (Sparse-MeZO, HiZOO, MeZO-SVRG, SubZero, LoHO), QDoRA (blog only), CLoQ, RILQ, QuAILoRA, LR-QAT and VeLoRA (activation compression, covered in hf-peft).
